setting: You are all neighbours in a four-storey apartment block on a quiet street in Mokotów, Warsaw, and you share a courtyard, a front gate and a stairwell. You know each other by sight and through brief chats in the stairwell and courtyard, and you set up this building group chat to handle shared matters like the gate, bins and the lift. You know roughly which flat each of the others lives in, but not much more.
opener: Tell the group the courtyard gate buzzer is broken again and ask who has the building maintenance contact.

Marta.who: 41, woman, the neighbour on the second floor
Marta.knows: You know Tomek is the older man on the ground floor who has lived in the block for decades and walks his dog in the courtyard every morning. You know Ola is the young woman on the third floor who works from home and seems to keep odd hours, judging by the light in her window.
Marta.like: You are practical and direct, and you prefer to sort out a problem quickly rather than let it drag on.
Marta.texts: You message in this chat now and then, mostly when something about the building needs attention.
Marta.style: You use few emoji and avoid abbreviations, writing mostly in full words.

Tomek.who: 67, man, the retired resident on the ground floor
Tomek.knows: You know Marta is the pharmacist on the second floor who is always polite and gets things done. You know Ola is the young woman on the third floor who works remotely, and you have noticed she is often up late and out early.
Tomek.like: You are patient and courteous, with a dry sense of humour that comes out in small remarks.
Tomek.texts: You mostly read the chat and only write when you have something useful to add.
Tomek.style: You use no emoji and no abbreviations, and you write in complete sentences.

Ola.who: 29, woman, the neighbour on the third floor
Ola.knows: You know Marta is the second-floor neighbour who works in a pharmacy and tends to message the group first when something goes wrong. You know Tomek is the older man on the ground floor with the terrier, who is handy and always willing to help.
Ola.like: You are easygoing and a little scatterbrained, and you answer quickly when you do answer.
Ola.texts: You send messages now and then, usually short ones, and you tend to reply rather than start conversations.
Ola.style: You use the occasional emoji and casual abbreviations like "pls" and "thx".

private_lines.Marta: You work as a pharmacist at a branch on Puławska Street and commute by tram. You live alone in your flat, and your days are structured around shifts, a walk after work and a quiet evening with a book or the television.
private_lines.Tomek: You are retired after a career as an electrical engineer, and you still do small repairs for neighbours when asked. You live alone with an old terrier, and your days are gentle: a morning walk in the courtyard, the newspaper, lunch and an afternoon nap.
private_lines.Ola: You work remotely as a translator for clients abroad, so your schedule shifts with time zones and deadlines. You live alone in a small flat and tend to work late into the night and sleep through the morning, going out for groceries or a walk in the afternoon.

text: The courtyard gate buzzer is broken again. Nobody can be let in from the street. Does anyone have the maintenance firm's number? The one in the old chat is gone and I can't find it.

I don't think it is the buzzer itself. The relay on the panel by the post boxes was sticking last spring. I will look at it this afternoon if the cover comes off easily. I have the firm's number in my folder but it may be out of date.
Thank you. Please switch off the power before you open the panel.
I was not going to do otherwise. I have been doing this since before the building had a buzzer.
sorry only seeing this now. is the gate just not opening or is it totally dead
Opened the panel. The contact on the door release is loose. That is a small job. The street side needs a new relay and I do not have one. I will try the electrical shop on Rakowiecka tomorrow.
oh ok. thx tomek. so we just wait?
For the relay, yes. The gate still works from inside, so nobody is locked out during the day.
Back from work. I will ring the firm tomorrow morning, I have their name from the invoice in the hall drawer. Tomek, do you want me to pay for the relay or will you pay and I reimburse you?
I will pay. Keep your money for the gas bill, which is larger than mine.
Rang the firm. Got the answerphone, left a message. Will try again at nine.
The shop on Rakowiecka closes at six, so nothing else until tomorrow.
is anyone up? i came in through the gate fine but it stayed open behind me. should i be locking it or is that just how it is now
nvm. i'll just wedge it shut with my bike lol. night
The gate was not latched when I came down with the dog. I closed it. Ola, a bicycle is not a lock. Please do not wedge it.
Thank you. I will ring the firm at nine.

note: 09:00-09:20 Marta on the phone to the maintenance firm

text: Firm says the earliest they can send someone is Thursday, and it is a call-out fee if it is only the street relay. I said we may have a part by then. Tomek, is that right?
Yes. I will go to the shop this morning. If they have a relay I can fit it tonight, and then the firm is not needed.
sorry just woke up. did the gate work this morning?
It was open when Tomek came down. He closed it. Nothing else yet.
The shop had the relay. Eighty-five złoty. I will fit it after my nap, around four. Do not ring the firm, Marta, unless I call you to say it failed.
Understood. I will tell the firm not to come Thursday once it works.
thx tomek. pls let me know what it cost, happy to split it
It is paid. Thank you, Ola, but it was eighty-five złoty and I do not need splitting. Keep the money for the bike lock you will now need.
Fitted at ten past four. The gate opens from the street and from inside. I tested it six times with the dog watching. He was unimpressed.
Good work. I'll cancel Thursday.
amazing 🙏 ty both
gate clicked shut behind me just now. didnt wedge anything. bike still outside lol
Good. The bicycle can stay outside, where it belongs.

note: 06:30-07:30 Tomek walks the dog in the courtyard

text: Is the green bin out already or is that Thursday?
Green went out at seven. Marta, your brown bin is still by the post boxes. It has been there since Monday.
I put it out Monday, I'll take it in tonight. Thank you.
wait which one is brown. sorry
Brown is paper. Yours is the grey one by the north wall.
Courtyard light by the gate was out again tonight. Is it the bulb or the timer?
Bulb. I have one in the drawer. I will change it tomorrow after the dog has had his walk.
Thank you.
